newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Underperforming the bloc.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Underperforming the bloc.

text.p: The Australian bond market underperformed against the dollar bloc, particularly against the short end of the U.S. curve, as its showed slight disappointment on two fronts, analysts said.

The first was when the Reserve Bank left policy unchanged after Tuesday's board meeting, although an easing was only seen as an extreme outside chance, and secondly that today's release of first quarter GDP came in much in line with expectations.
March quarter GDP rose 0.9 percent when some analysts had been looking for a weaker outcome to maintain the recent strong bond rally.

The short end is seen being slightly at risk after the recent strong rally, which had taken three-year lows to a 3-1/4 lows and a negative spread to the U.S., particularly in front of Friday's U.S. labour force data and the local long holiday week with markets closed here on Monday.
The long-end still remains near a key resistance level on the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread.

"Continuing offshore and domestic support and the modest outlook for growth is likely to keep the 10-year Aussie/U.S. spread in the 70-90 basis point range in the near-term," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank.
"However, 65 basis points is a key resistance level, and if broken, has the potential to see the Aussie market outperform towards 50 basis points," she added.
